about: Question design for the Assignment 02 pilot (ECE 2514). Main questions are predict and tracing only, one per function, the type rotating by form. what-if is a follow-up prepared for every function (see followUp). Fields "spec" (predict answers) and "refStops" (the reference's trace stops, used only to choose a K for targeted inputs) are filled by run-all.js by running code. Do not edit them by hand. There is no spec answer for tracing: the answer is the student's own trace.
placeholders: Main questions: {input} = the input's "display" text; tracing also {line} (the student's breakpoint line, pauseLine in meta.json), {function}, {kth} ("1st", "2nd", ..., chosen per student from their own trace) and {what} (per function, tracing.what). Follow-up: {line}, {find}, {replace}, {function}, {input}.
tracingQuestion: You put a breakpoint on line {line} and run {function} on {input}. When it stops for the {kth} time, {what}?
backup: mode is the backup. It replaces a function that cannot be asked (for example a tracing question when the function has no line to put a breakpoint on) and takes the type of the function it replaces.

followUp.question: If you changed line {line} of your code from `{find}` to `{replace}`, what would your {function} return for {input}?
followUp.questionReverseList: If you changed line {line} of your code from `{find}` to `{replace}`, what would the vector hold after reverseList runs on {input}?
followUp.when: Asked only after a correct main answer (engine rule comes in M4). The answer comes from running the student's changed copy.
rules: The what-if output must differ from the student's plain output on the chosen input.
If the student's plain output differs from the spec answer, the what-if output must not equal the spec answer (the change must never be the fix).
If no line passes both checks, the what-if is skipped for that function and the reason is logged.

inputRules: An input where the code crashes, gives a runtime error or hits the time limit is never used (undefined behavior). The next separating input is used; if none, a standard input with targeted = false.

playCraps inputs whose answer depends on the validation reading in SPEC-NOTES.md (an invalid value after the game is already decided) have unclearSpec = true and are not used until the spec is confirmed.
Inputs that end with a delimiter, and playCraps inputs with an odd number of values, are never used (not defined by the spec).
